revisions.summary: The intention: The faint clock hangs in the air. Each echo brings it a little closer until the singer and the drums can pass the beat between them at ground level. The bass at eighteen seconds pulls the whole ride forward in shallow strokes. It coasts over the missing weight at twenty-seven, then slowly gets its bounce back as the high sound comes through over the motor.

The intention: Start with a nearly flat glide under the faint ticks. Let the brighter calls pull it into small, hanging arcs. Build speed through the tight upper tune, then let the drum replies lean forward between softer words. Hit the bass return hard and hold a low, quick run. The hollow beat halfway through lets the rider lift and ease off. Bring the pulse back under that wider bounce, then gather speed and flatten the jumps as the cut approaches.

The intention: A machine winding up. The faint clock is a slow pendulum: every tick the same small swing, and the calls swing a little wider. The four-note figure and the words and drum replies stay close and quick. Then the low motor takes over for half a minute, and the whole passage is one gesture: it starts as tall, slow, heavy piston strokes and, stroke by stroke, runs lower and faster, until by the cut it is a fast flat hum along the line. The one hollow stroke is a hiccup: the rider rolls through it instead of bouncing, then picks the rhythm up again. The approved reading rides the motor at one constant pace and height; this one gives it a direction. Strengths as approved.

The intention: A machine that stalls once and winds itself back up. From Opus: the faint clock is a slow pendulum, every tick the same small swing, and the calls swing a little wider; the four-note figure and the words with their drum replies stay close and quick. From Sol: the motor's first stroke is the hardest landing of the film. From the approved reading: the low motor ridden as one even run of high, fast strokes, which its ride shows cleanly (lower and flatter versions of the motor picked up stray touches). Its own: the hollow stroke halfway is a stall. As in Sol the rider lifts over it and loses its pace; then the motor restarts in slow, tall strokes and winds back up, a little faster and flatter each bar, until it is back at full speed for the last third of the ride. Strengths as approved otherwise.
This is the blend, the main reading of the song since 2026-11-19. Nothing changed in it.
Nothing changed in the reading: it is the one approved before the blend took its place as the main reading.
